_about: What Knos can do and how far each thing has got. `stage` is the highest of `stages` that has evidence; scripts/capabilities.py checks the evidence (offline, and against devnet with --rpc) and renders the table in README.md. An exercised signature that no document of this repository gives is left out and filled by the release; nothing is `reproduced` until a document links someone else's run. Only a public program id is evidence for `deployed` and `exercised`: the `knos_*` addresses of programs-v2/program_ids.json and upgrade_gate's own `declare_id!`, each listed under `programs` with the version devnet runs there (`on_chain`). A deployment of a build at an address of its own (the 0.3.14 rehearsal's staging programs) is never evidence: what ran there is said in the capability's note, with its transaction, and the capability stays `tested` until a transaction at a public id exercises it. docs/CAPABILITIES.md lists the rehearsal's transactions.

capabilities.what: A pull request's claims about its tests and CI are checked against GitHub's own check runs, free.
capabilities.note: Runs in GitHub Actions and on the author's machine: there is no program to deploy.

capabilities.what: One link opens a pull request that installs Knos in a repository, with no secret.
capabilities.note: The link is built and checked here; no outside repository is known to have installed by it.

capabilities.what: Five terms templates give a funding comment and the exact terms it funds.
capabilities.note: The hashes are made with sample facts; a repository's own are in the reply to its comment.

capabilities.what: Before a coding agent stops, a hook checks what it says is done against the repository.
An MCP server gives a coding agent the check, the terms and the order tools.
An agent with its own key finds funded work, takes it, submits it after the local check passes, and collects.
capabilities.note: Tested against stand-ins for GitHub and the chain; on the rehearsal's staging deployment an agent found, took and submitted an auto order with these tools and was paid (order_auto_accept). The tools that post are off until the operator turns them on.

capabilities.what: A program on Solana verifies a GitHub Actions OpenID Connect token and other programs read the result.
The same program verifies a gitlab.com CI token under GitLab's own, longer key.
A key of any RS256 issuer is admitted on GitHub's signature and its tokens are verified.
capabilities.note: Waits for the upgrade to `knos_pay 2.1` and `knos_oidc 2.1`, which has not executed.

capabilities.what: A guardian multisig approves or revokes a signing key and can do nothing else.
One comment on an issue funds a task from the repository owner's Balance.
A wallet funds a task with its own money.
A merge that GitHub signs pays the author of the pull request.
A payee with no wallet is held for, and paid once they bind a wallet from their own repository.
With no proof by the deadline the money goes back where it came from.
The guardian pauses new funding for a limited time and money in escrow still leaves.
A work order fixes its checks, paths, payees and deadline as a hash at funding, and the funder pays the fee on top.

capabilities.what: An order funded as auto pays the first pull request its black-box suite passes, with no merge and no person's step.
capabilities.note: Rehearsed on a staging deployment of the knos_pay 2.1 build (signature 9zUVa8nkpCuizDnLNVZCVVS8FPPoEy6KhXz8RYDUPHH2vNEcvD9fuBtrSTxDKhTNi84e6yuMGcoj6uNAxuaeECd; docs/CAPABILITIES.md, "The 0.3.14 rehearsal on devnet"), not on the public program ids: the public knos_pay and knos_oidc carry it only once their upgrade to 2.1 has executed, and no transaction there is recorded yet. An agent found, took and submitted the work through the MCP tools, and its pull request was accepted with no merge; the payment was held for the account until its wallet was bound, then paid. The funder chooses it at funding, and only for an order paid by the black-box suite.

capabilities.what: A neutral run that finds the paid head failing, sent inside the order's warranty, returns the holdback to the funder.
capabilities.note: Rehearsed on a staging deployment of the knos_pay 2.1 build (signature 5H6mrHjgLhRxgFNWLa8p1R5BVhgzsU22Yj2b6AGbqzANCiaHLKRN6XuVYziRaTiQaqTL4pFwpfTnnRMS3csi3EL5; docs/CAPABILITIES.md, "The 0.3.14 rehearsal on devnet"), not on the public program ids: the public knos_pay and knos_oidc carry it only once their upgrade to 2.1 has executed, and no transaction there is recorded yet. The neutral run came from another repository than the order's, inside the warranty; it signed because the paid pull request's merge had been reverted, not by running the checks on the head again. Only what the order still holds returns: what was paid at acceptance stays paid, and after the warranty no challenge is heard.

capabilities.what: An order with a quorum pays only when two or three distinct judges passed the same artifact.

A `quorum 2` order recorded its first judge, then paid on the second.

capabilities.what: Anyone can run the relay that carries signed tokens to the chain.
capabilities.note: Runs in GitHub Actions: there is no program to deploy.

capabilities.what: Adapter workflows turn a signed event (a release, a deployment, an attestation, a tracker's webhook) into a settlement or a count.

capabilities.what: A canary funds and pays one order in a round and fails when the payment does not land in five minutes.
1,000 orders open at once are each paid once and none is lost.

capabilities.what: The instruction handlers of the four programs are driven from Rust against the built binaries.

capabilities.what: Kani harnesses state that an order's amount and fee are exactly what the payees, the relayer and the fee owner receive.
capabilities.note: Proved only where `cargo kani` runs (the program workflow's kani job); no test of this repository runs Kani, and no run on this build is recorded here. `cargo test` runs the same properties on random inputs.

capabilities.what: A paid order gives a receipt that anyone can check against the chain.
An evidence bundle holds what an order's verdict follows from, and verifies with no network.
capabilities.note: Built from a replayed chain in the tests; no bundle of a devnet order is published.

capabilities.what: A mirror of receipts keeps what the chain's history no longer serves, and verifies against the chain.
capabilities.note: Tested on a replayed chain; no public mirror runs.

An `x402` server takes a Knos order as payment for a resource.

capabilities.what: An organisation exports every order of a period as one hash-chained file that two parties can compare.

capabilities.what: A public index counts how often an agent's pull request says its checks pass when one had failed.
The index gives each agent's rate of failed checks by week.
capabilities.note: Computed from the committed sample and from a capped scan read on 5 Oct 2026, cut by week; the weekly job opens a pull request and merges nothing.

capabilities.what: A command lists what must be true before mainnet and fails while any line is not.
A deliverable is an order and a milestone, and it is one accepted outcome whatever number of pull requests carried it.
capabilities.note: Off chain, in the ledger a statement is made from; no program was changed for it.

capabilities.what: A wrong verdict or a withdrawal is netted by a correction anchored under a leaf of its own, and the statement names who issued it.

capabilities.what: A month is closed off chain when both ledgers agree after repeats and corrections, each side signs the close with a GitHub run of its own, and no real close has been signed yet.

capabilities.what: The same evidence sent again is not another evaluation: the ledger keeps the first and lists every repeat with its reason.
A receipt keeps five things apart: the identity the issuer authenticated, the execution evidence, the acceptance policy, the commercial authorisation, and what remains trusted.
capabilities.note: Receipt version 3; versions 1 and 2 still check.

capabilities.what: A receipt records whether each evaluator's run was the buyer's own, the seller's own or neither, computed from the ids the issuer signed.
capabilities.note: A record of who ran the evaluation, not a judgment that the evaluator is honest.

capabilities.what: `knos bundle verify --no-chain` checks a bundle with no cluster and says what the signatures prove, what is an archived copy, and what needs a cluster.
capabilities.note: What survives a devnet reset is the issuer's signature and the archived copies; that the payment happened is then an archived copy, and the output says so.
